verdict.rationale: Hatchet's GitHub README says the platform provides automatic retries, and the docs include a "Retry Policies" page, so retries are a documented first-party capability. The pack holds only that one claim plus a page title, with no detail on how retries are configured. The founder's remark that you can't try/catch a single task reflects Hatchet's declared-ahead workflow design and does not contradict automatic retries. Missing for 10: configurable backoff, per-step timeouts, failure policies (e.g. on-failure handlers), detailed retry-configuration docs, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a backend developer, every step retries automatically with configurable backoff, timeouts, and failure policies — no try/catch scaffolding

citations.quote: Hatchet provides a full platform for queuing, automatic retries, durability, real-time monitoring, alerting, and logging.
